lots.key_photo_findings: Confirmed from all 15 photos. Photo 1: full view matches the description. Photos 5, 6, 9, 10, 14: drawer fronts show strong birdseye and burr figure consistent with Huon pine; carcass sides and top are plainer pine-type timber with knots (photo 8), which is normal for Huon pine pieces. Crest and finials (photos 2, 3, 7) look a slightly redder, possibly stained, tone. Photo 11: a chunk of timber missing and an old patch at a drawer top edge near the lock. Photos 12-13: lock mortice exposed with wood loss and an old repair on another drawer. Photos 14-15: aluminium or tin strips fitted inside a drawer as runners or liners (later addition). Photo 8: scratches and wear on the top. No maker's mark or label seen.
lots.condition: Fair to good, honest used condition: drawer lock area damage and old repairs, later metal strips in a drawer, surface wear on the top, finish worn in places. Mirror glass condition not shown close up.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the whole carcass Huon pine or only the drawer fronts? Is the mirror glass original and free of silvering loss, and do all drawers run freely? Any keys?

lots.key_photo_findings: Crops of photos 3 and 4 enlarged. Spoon 1: maker's mark in a rectangle reading roughly 'L.F.N' or 'I.F.N' (not confidently legible, maker not identified), lowercase h in a cut-corner cartouche, lion passant in a shaped cartouche, crowned leopard's head in a shield. The crowned leopard dates it before 1821 and, with an Old English pattern (downturned end, no Hanoverian rib) and no sovereign's head duty mark, fits London 1783-84 as Gowans says. Spoon 2: the same style h and punch shapes, but the maker's mark looks different (reads roughly 'B.?.L'), and the lion and leopard are worn almost flat, so this is probably a made-up pair of the same year by different makers. Photos 1-2: both bowls show wear and scratches; no dents, splits or engraving seen, but the bowl tips are not shown close up.
lots.condition: Worn but sound in photos: rubbed marks on spoon 2, general scratching to the bowls, no visible damage. Probably a matched pair rather than a true pair.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm the weight of each spoon, whether both maker's marks match or differ, and whether there is any bowl tip wear, splits, repairs or removed engraving (thin spots) on either spoon.
